title: Risk assessment: Namespace .egg-state files per-pipeline
summary: The proposed change (Approach A — prefix filenames with issue/pipeline identifier) is well-scoped and follows an established codebase convention. The primary risks relate to missed callsites and in-flight pipeline backward compatibility, both of which are mitigable. One significant gap in the architect's analysis: the orchestrator/handoffs.py and orchestrator/dispatch.py wrapper modules were not listed as files requiring changes, but they call the shared load/save functions and need identifier plumbing. The risk of this change causing production incidents is low because all enforcement layers (gateway, phase filter, readonly mounts) use directory-level wildcards that are transparent to file renames.

architect_analysis_review.accuracy: Mostly accurate with one notable gap
architect_analysis_review.gap_identified: The architect's key_files list and implementation plan omit orchestrator/handoffs.py (wraps load_agent_output/save_agent_output/collect_handoff_data with ORM types), orchestrator/dispatch.py (calls save_agent_output at line 219 and collect_handoff_data at line 264), and orchestrator/routes/signals.py (calls handoffs.save_agent_output at line 193). These wrapper layers need identifier plumbing to pass through to the underlying shared functions.
correct_claims: Gateway uses directory-level wildcards — no gateway changes needed (verified: gateway/phase_filter.py:495 uses '.egg-state/agent-outputs/*')
Readonly mounts don't cover agent-outputs/ or checks/ (verified: _IMPLEMENT_READONLY_DIRS only has drafts, contracts, pipelines, reviews)
Health check at phase_output.py:152 scans directory via iterdir() — works with any filename (verified)
_build_autofix_prompt is deprecated and never called — only prompt strings reference implement-results.json (verified: no callers found)
implement-results.json has no programmatic reader in the orchestrator — the orchestrator passes check_results as a dict parameter to _build_autofix_prompt, which is itself dead code
architect_analysis_review.recommendation: Add orchestrator/handoffs.py, orchestrator/dispatch.py, and orchestrator/routes/signals.py to the implementation plan as additional files requiring changes. The handoffs module is the primary interface used by the orchestrator for agent output I/O.

risks.title: Missed wrapper callsites in orchestrator/handoffs.py and dispatch.py
risks.description: The architect's plan updates shared/egg_contracts/orchestrator.py (load_agent_output, save_agent_output, collect_handoff_data) to accept an identifier parameter, but orchestrator/handoffs.py wraps ALL three of these functions with its own save_agent_output(), load_agent_output_data(), and collect_handoff_data(). orchestrator/dispatch.py:219 calls save_agent_output() and dispatch.py:264 calls collect_handoff_data() through these wrappers. orchestrator/routes/signals.py:193 calls handoffs.save_agent_output(). If the wrapper layer is not updated to accept and forward the identifier, the underlying shared functions will receive identifier=None and fall back to the old global paths, silently defeating the entire fix.
risks.mitigation: Add identifier parameter to all wrapper functions in orchestrator/handoffs.py. Update dispatch.py and signals.py callers to pass pipeline context (issue_number or pipeline_id). The identifier is already available in the pipeline object at these callsites.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert to old global paths — since the shared functions have identifier=None as default, reverting just the wrapper changes restores old behavior.

risks.title: In-flight pipeline backward compatibility during rollout
risks.description: When this change is deployed, there may be in-flight pipelines that have already written agent outputs to old global paths (e.g., architect-output.json). If the readers are updated to look for prefixed paths first without a fallback, those in-flight pipelines will fail to find their dependency outputs and produce incomplete or incorrect results.
risks.mitigation: The architect correctly proposes backward-compatible fallback: try new prefixed path first, fall back to old global path. This is the right approach. The fallback code should be clearly marked with a TODO for removal after all in-flight pipelines complete (approx 1-2 days after deployment).
risks.rollback_plan: Revert to main. In-flight pipelines on old code will continue to work since they use the old paths.

risks.title: Agent sandbox commands reference hardcoded global filenames
risks.description: The sandbox agent mode commands (coder-mode.md, tester-mode.md, integrator-mode.md, documenter-mode.md) contain hardcoded file paths like 'cat .egg-state/agent-outputs/coder-output.json' and 'cat > .egg-state/agent-outputs/tester-output.json'. However, these are only used in manual/interactive agent mode, not in pipeline-spawned agents. Pipeline-spawned agents receive their output path from _build_agent_prompt() which will be updated. The sandbox commands are used when a developer manually runs a skill like /tester-mode.
risks.mitigation: Update sandbox commands to use dynamically constructed paths based on $EGG_ISSUE_NUMBER. Since these commands are markdown templates, they can use shell variable interpolation. Alternatively, since manual mode is rare and the backward-compat fallback covers reads, this could be deferred.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert the sandbox command changes. Manual mode users will continue using old paths.

risks.title: Identifier unavailable in local/non-issue pipeline modes
risks.description: In local pipeline mode (no issue number), the identifier must be derived from pipeline_id. If pipeline_id is also None (e.g., direct CLI invocation without a pipeline), the code must have a sensible fallback. The architect mentions falling back to 'local' which matches the pattern in _get_draft_path().
risks.mitigation: Follow the existing pattern from _get_draft_path(): use issue_number for issue mode, pipeline_id for pipeline mode, 'local' as final fallback. This is already proposed in AD-4.
risks.rollback_plan: N/A — low risk with clear pattern to follow.

risks.title: Integration test hardcoded path in phase-runner.sh
risks.description: integration_tests/local_pipeline/mock-sandbox/phase-runner.sh:143 writes to RESULTS_FILE="$CHECKS_DIR/implement-results.json" with a hardcoded filename. After the change, the orchestrator prompts will tell agents to write to a prefixed filename, but the mock sandbox script still writes to the old name. This will cause integration tests to either fail or not properly test the new behavior.
risks.mitigation: Update phase-runner.sh to derive the filename from EGG_ISSUE_NUMBER or EGG_PIPELINE_ID environment variables, which are already available in the sandbox environment. E.g., RESULTS_FILE="$CHECKS_DIR/${EGG_ISSUE_NUMBER:-local}-implement-results.json"

risks.title: Prompt-agent path mismatch if agents ignore prompt instructions
risks.description: Agent output file paths are communicated to agents via prompt instructions (e.g., 'Write your analysis to .egg-state/agent-outputs/871-architect-output.json'). If an agent writes to a different path (e.g., the old global path), the programmatic readers won't find the output at the expected prefixed path. The backward-compat fallback mitigates this for the transition period, but after fallback removal, a misbehaving agent could silently lose output.
risks.mitigation: The backward-compat fallback handles this during transition. Long-term, this is an existing risk (agents can already write to wrong paths) and is not introduced by this change. Consider keeping the fallback permanently as a safety net, or adding a health check that warns when output is found at the fallback path.
risks.rollback_plan: Keep backward-compat fallback in place permanently rather than removing it.

risks.title: Test coverage for wrapper module changes
risks.description: The architect's test plan (TASK-5-1 through TASK-5-6) covers orchestrator tests for prompt assertions, health checks, and backward-compat fallback. However, it does not mention tests for orchestrator/handoffs.py, orchestrator/dispatch.py, or orchestrator/routes/signals.py. The test at orchestrator/tests/test_signals.py:86 mocks save_agent_output — it would need updating if the function signature changes.
risks.mitigation: Add test_signals.py to the test update list. Verify that dispatch.py and handoffs.py have existing tests and update them if so.

security_assessment.details: This change is purely a file naming convention update within the .egg-state directory. No new input validation, authentication, authorization, or data handling code is introduced. The gateway and phase filter enforcement layers are unaffected (they use directory-level wildcards). No new file paths are constructed from user input — the identifier comes from issue_number (integer) or pipeline_id (server-generated string), both of which are trusted internal values.

performance_assessment.details: The backward-compat fallback adds one additional file existence check (os.path.exists) per read when the new prefixed file doesn't exist. This is a negligible cost — one stat() syscall. No new I/O patterns, database queries, or network calls are introduced.

steps: Since the shared functions default to identifier=None (backward compat), reverting writers restores old global paths

Any in-flight pipelines on the new code that already wrote prefixed files will have those files ignored by the reverted code, but the backward-compat fallback in readers means they'd still be read if the fallback code is present
Clean approach: revert the entire PR. In-flight pipelines may need manual intervention to restart, but this is a standard pipeline failure recovery.
rollback_plan.estimated_blast_radius: Low — only affects .egg-state file I/O within the SDLC pipeline. No production code, gateway enforcement, or user-facing behavior is impacted.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The architect's plan omits this file. The implementation must add identifier parameter threading through save_agent_output(), load_agent_output_data(), collect_handoff_data(), and get_handoff_env_var(). Reviewer should verify all callers (dispatch.py, signals.py) pass the identifier correctly.

The architect proposes removing the fallback after in-flight pipelines complete. The reviewer should decide whether to keep it permanently as a safety net (minor code debt) or remove it after a defined period. Recommendation: keep it — the cost is one stat() call per read, and it protects against agent misbehavior.

The sandbox commands use static markdown with hardcoded paths. Converting to dynamic paths requires shell variable interpolation in markdown templates. Reviewer should verify the template rendering mechanism supports this, or consider whether to leave sandbox commands on old paths (since they're only used in manual interactive mode and the fallback covers reads).

conditions: Add orchestrator/handoffs.py, orchestrator/dispatch.py, and orchestrator/routes/signals.py to the implementation plan with specific tasks for identifier plumbing
Add orchestrator/tests/test_signals.py to the test update list
Consider keeping backward-compat fallback permanently rather than planning removal
Ensure integration test phase-runner.sh is updated to use identifier-prefixed filename
